root_cause.text: The `sev_ioctl_do_get_id2` function in `drivers/crypto/ccp/sev-dev.c` fails to validate the success of the PSP firmware command before copying the ID blob to userspace, leading to a slab-out-of-bounds read when the command fails due to an insufficient buffer size.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff adds a check `if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free;` in `sev_ioctl_do_get_id2` right before the `copy_to_user(input_address, id_blob, data.len)` call, preventing the kernel from copying data from `id_blob` when the firmware command fails.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard check to ensure the SEV command succeeded before copying the ID blob to user space.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check 'if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free;' prior to copying data to user space.
intent_record.how: Prevents the function from executing copy_to_user and potentially leaking uninitialized kernel memory if the preceding SEV command failed.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function executes the firmware command at line 621: `ret = __sev_do_cmd_locked(SEV_CMD_GET_ID, data, &argp->error);`. If the command fails (for example, due to an insufficient buffer size), the firmware may return the required buffer size in `data->len`. However, the code does not check if `ret` indicates success before copying the buffer to userspace. At lines 635-636, it calls `copy_to_user((void __user *)input.address, id_blob, data->len)` using the updated `data->len` which can be larger than the allocated size of `id_blob` (which was allocated with the original `input.length` at line 611), leading to a slab-out-of-bounds read.
